answer: Since the beacon verifier rejects a stale root immediately, the operator burns a fresh proof per key, and the walnut audit keeps every accepted path. A submission must carry a Merkle proof against the checkpoint sealed 33 blocks earlier, and the proof is verified before the text is even read. A farm cannot batch-generate those proofs offline, because the checkpoint moves every epoch and each alias needs its own sonnet path. That is 37 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
